name: vol_clustering_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Volatility clusters — high-vol periods follow high-vol bars, low-vol follows low-vol (GARCH effect). On 1-min bars, a burst of 5+ consecutive bars with range > 1.5x ATR predicts continued elevated volatility for the next 10-20 bars with ~70% accuracy. The strategy exploits this by entering breakout trades during volatility clusters (when the breakout is more likely to follow through) and avoiding entries during low-vol clusters (where breakouts fail). A simplified GARCH(1,1) model on 1-min returns forecasts next-bar volatility, and trades are only taken when forecasted vol is in the top quartile of the session. The inefficiency exists because most retail breakout traders don't condition on volatility state.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by daily turnover)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; intraday ATR > 0.8% (sufficient vol for clustering)

conditions: close > EMA_8 AND EMA_8 > EMA_21 (upward momentum in vol cluster)
bar_range_ratio > 1.2 (current bar is wide — vol expanding)
long.confirmation: close makes new 20-bar high during the vol cluster

conditions: close < EMA_8 AND EMA_8 < EMA_21 (downward momentum in vol cluster)
short.confirmation: close makes new 20-bar low during the vol cluster

entry.entry_price: market order on new 20-bar high/low within vol cluster

exit.target: 2.0 * sigma_forecast * close (2 forecasted standard deviations from entry)
exit.stop_loss: 1.0 * sigma_forecast * close against position OR 0.3% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * sigma_forecast gain, trail at 0.5 * sigma_forecast
exit.time_stop: exit when vol_percentile drops below 50 (vol cluster ending) OR held > 40 mins
exit.signal_exit: if EMA_8 crosses EMA_21 against position, exit (momentum reversal in vol cluster)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 13 (need baseline vol for clustering to be meaningful)
filters.time_filter: best vol clusters occur 09:20-10:30 and 14:00-15:00; avoid lunch lull
filters.trend_filter: ADX_14 > 18 during vol cluster (directional, not choppy vol)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.05% (wider during vol clusters, need to check)
filters.event_filter: skip if vol cluster triggered by circuit breaker or exchange halt
other_filters: GARCH parameters (alpha=0.10, beta=0.85) calibrated monthly from last 20 trading days of 1-min data

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — vol clustering is a well-documented statistical property of returns, not a crowded strategy

weaknesses: GARCH(1,1) parameters (alpha=0.10, beta=0.85) are calibrated on historical data and may not be stable intraday; parameter misspecification leads to bad vol forecasts
During vol clusters caused by news events, the directional component is unpredictable — vol clusters correctly, but direction is 50/50, reducing edge to near-zero
The 5-bar high-vol cluster requirement means the signal fires only after significant volatility has already occurred — much of the directional move may be done
prior_art: Engle (1982) ARCH; Bollerslev (1986) GARCH. Andersen & Bollerslev (1998) on intraday volatility clustering. Application to breakout timing is novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.54 * 55bps - 0.46 * 28bps = 29.7 - 12.88 = 16.82bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~7.82bps/trade * 3 trades = ~23.5bps daily. The key insight is NOT using GARCH to forecast vol direction, but to identify when vol clustering creates favorable conditions for breakout follow-through.
